metadata.title: CVE-2012-1148 on Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (focal) - low

metadata.title: CVE-2024-42516 on Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (focal) - medium

metadata.title: CVE-2025-4598 on Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (focal) - medium
metadata.description: A vulnerability was found in systemd-coredump. This flaw allows an attacker to force a SUID process to crash and replace it with a non-SUID binary to access the original's privileged process coredump, allowing the attacker to read sensitive data, such as /etc/shadow content, loaded by the original process. A SUID binary or process has a special type of permission, which allows the process to run with the file owner's permissions, regardless of the user executing the binary. This allows the process to access more restricted data than unprivileged users or processes would be able to. An attacker can leverage this flaw by forcing a SUID process to crash and force the Linux kernel to recycle the process PID before systemd-coredump can analyze the /proc/pid/auxv file. If the attacker wins the race condition, they gain access to the original's SUID process coredump file. They can read sensitive content loaded into memory by the original binary, affecting data confidentiality. Update Instructions: Run `sudo pro fix CVE-2025-4598` to fix the vulnerability. The problem can be corrected by updating your system to the following package versions: libnss-myhostname - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 libnss-mymachines - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 libnss-resolve - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 libnss-systemd - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 libpam-systemd - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 libsystemd0 - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 libudev1 - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 systemd - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 systemd-container - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 systemd-coredump - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 systemd-journal-remote - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 systemd-sysv - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 systemd-tests - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 systemd-timesyncd - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 udev - 245.4-4ubuntu3.24+esm1 Available with Ubuntu Pro (Infra-only): https://ubuntu.com/pro
